key_insight: The paper shows that arbitrary single-qubit gates can be synthesized in constant depth using only unitary operations, and that bounded-width circuits fundamentally require Θ(log log(1/ε)) depth.
engineering_relevance: This tightens the depth-cost tradeoff for quantum compilation and identifies when larger multi-qubit gates can collapse synthesis depth to constant time.
method: Constructs an ε-approximate single-qubit synthesis using Hadamard, T, generalized Toffoli, and clean ancillae.
Eliminates the need for pre-supplied catalysts and later removes Fan-Out entirely.
Provides a depth-preserving real simulation of bounded-error QAC circuits using only Hadamard, X, and generalized Toffoli gates.
evidence_signal: The abstract claims both an O(log log(1/ε)) upper bound for bounded-width gates and a matching Ω(log log(1/ε)) lower bound, plus a depth-O(d) simulation result for depth-d QAC circuits.
watch_item: Practical use may be limited by the need for generalized Toffoli gates of substantial width and many clean ancillae, which can be costly on near-term hardware.
